commitResults.messageBody: Move command input, greetings, errors, task feedback, and dividers behind a dedicated Ui class. This gives console presentation a single responsibility while preserving all existing command behavior and leaves parsing and task-list extraction for later increments.

commitResults.messageBody:
The Java classes use the default package, which does not follow the
project coding standard and weakens source organization.

Move production and test classes into the otaku package, update the
Gradle entry point, and extract the repeated event format error so the
affected lines remain within the standard's length limit.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add task search by description keyword
commitResults.messageBody:
Users cannot narrow the task list when looking for a specific item.

Add a find command that validates its keyword and displays matching task
descriptions in list order. Cover matching, missing keywords, no matches,
and unchanged task state with unit and UI tests.

Add cross-platform JavaFX dependencies and tests for response state and persistence.

Command parsing and task construction rely on invariants that are easy
to overlook when the code changes. Violations indicate programming errors
rather than invalid user input.

Add Java assertions at those boundaries so development runs fail early
with messages that explain each assumption, while retaining the existing
runtime validation and user-facing errors.

The command dispatcher mixed high-level routing with parsing, mutation,
and output details, making the method difficult to scan and maintain.

Move each command workflow into a focused helper and use an explicit switch
for dispatch. This keeps each method at one abstraction level and makes the
main command path easier to follow without changing behavior.

Command handlers used numeric substring offsets tied to the spelling of each
command word. Those unexplained values obscure intent and can silently become
stale when command names change.

Centralize argument extraction and derive its boundary from CommandType.
This removes the magic offsets and gives every handler one consistent way to
obtain its arguments.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use a stream to identify command types
commitResults.messageBody:
Command recognition is a search for the first enum value whose word matches
the input. Expressing that search as a stream makes the selection and UNKNOWN
fallback explicit without introducing side effects.

Keep the matching rule in a named predicate so the stream pipeline remains
readable and command-word construction stays in one place.

Users cannot currently organize dated tasks into a useful schedule, and
manually comparing dates becomes cumbersome as the task list grows.

Add a sort command that orders deadlines by due date and events by start
date while placing todos last and preserving ties. Persist the result, reject
unsupported arguments, and document and test the complete behavior.
Bring the package organization and coding-standard guidance into master so the completed increment is represented in the main project history.
Bring task search and its automated and CLI coverage into master so the Level-9 increment is part of the submitted history.
Integrate the JavaFX interface, executable jar configuration, and refined package structure while preserving the Level-9 command behavior already present on master.

Integrate assertion checks that document internal assumptions in the main development line.

Error replies previously looked like ordinary chatbot messages, making
invalid commands easy to miss. Carry error status with command results
so the GUI can apply a distinct alert style without parsing message text.

Reduce redundant avatar space and let message bubbles adapt to the
window width for a clearer, more compact conversation layout.

Otaku's generic wording and purple interface did not reinforce a
distinct character. Present Otaku as an upbeat, anime-inspired
questkeeper through themed greetings, task phrases, and interface copy.

Use a midnight, cyan, and orange palette to give the GUI a recognizable
mission-control identity while retaining the existing error styling.

commitResults.messageTitle: Handle malformed commands and task data
commitResults.messageBody:
Commands with blank input, repeated parameters, or duplicate tasks could
previously produce unclear results or create unintended entries. Normalize
command whitespace and reject each invalid form with a focused message.

Require event end dates to be strictly later than start dates in both
commands and persisted data so invalid schedules cannot enter the task
list.

commitResults.messageTitle: Expand automated coverage across core behavior
commitResults.messageBody:
Command parsing and persistence still had important success, validation,
and I/O failure paths without focused regression tests. Add JUnit cases
for all commands, malformed task data, failed storage access, assertions,
and sorting edge cases.

Add JaCoCo reporting to quantify non-GUI coverage and document a manual
matrix for layout, scaling, locale, and platform checks. The new tests
also expose and fix an unhandled corrupted-date exception.

The repository still described Otaku as a template and produced an
artifact carrying the old Duke name. Replace the setup-only README with
product, command, testing, and execution guidance, including the required
AI-assistance and dependency acknowledgements.

Rename the executable artifact to otaku.jar so the product identity is
consistent in the interface, documentation, and distribution.

The product website needs a single full-window image that demonstrates
Otaku's identity and conversation design. Add a real JavaFX rendering
showing successful and invalid commands, and display it prominently in
the user guide.

Replace the placeholder avatar with a branded mascot while retaining a
distinct error indicator.

Align the startup banner with the course reference style and render ASCII
art separately from plain greeting text. This preserves spacing without
changing normal typography. Update the UI test expectations accordingly.

The existing guide only explains task sorting, leaving new users without
enough information to operate the rest of the application.

Document setup, every command, persistence, task notation, validation, and
error behavior in a concise user-focused guide suitable for GitHub Pages.
